method: Read all source; dnfile/dncil CIL disassembly with metadata token and user-string resolution; Rizin entry/import/section review; cleave facts including decoded strings; atomscan local/slow before and after. No specimen contacted a live service. Python was exercised only with a replacement requests module.

executable_review.identity: Unsigned CLR XClient.exe 1.0.0.0, XWorm lineage. No exact release or original registry package is established.
executable_review.damage: First 4096-byte zero range 0x730..0x1730 destroys entry point MethodDef 38 at 0x904, configuration initializer and connection/send bodies; 0x9730..0xb730 destroys part of CLR heaps. Many metadata names are blank. Randomized identifiers and dummy constant-return functions also survive. Damage cannot be attributed to a specific protector or intent. Runtime success is not established.
executable_review.dispatch: Method 116 at 0x1938: argument bytes -> M195 Rijndael transform -> M187 string conversion -> delimiter Split -> array[0] CompareString. Dynamic shell branch at 0x1ba1 passes array[1] and (0,0,-1) to the same MemberRef as shutdown.exe /f /s /t 0 at 0x1b48. Type namespace Microsoft.VisualBasic and signature 0004080e1181c90208 establish the Shell-shaped call despite its blank name.
executable_review.payload: Method 116 FM branch Base64-decodes array[1], calls transform M192, then M127. M127 at 0x2af8 loads supplied bytes, obtains the entry method, creates its declaring-type instance and calls MethodBase.Invoke. DW branch stages bytes in a generated temp filename, then uses a hidden PowerShell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File branch for .ps1 or reflected Process.Start. The new activation composite states co-occurrence, not an intermethod flow proof.
executable_review.capture: Method 116 $Cap branch obtains screen dimensions and calls the six-argument graphics copy with four zero origins, Size and SRCCOPY 0x00cc0020. It rescales to 256x156, Image.Save(stream,Jpeg), converts that same stream to an array, transforms/Base64-encodes it into response[4], concatenates and dispatches the same response array. The transport helper body is erased: new hostile rule belongs to collection/screenshot and asserts response construction, not successful exfiltration.
executable_review.dos: Method 120 at 0x2728 starts 20 threads per round, waits 5 seconds and repeats under a time limit. Method 161 at 0x2b74 connects a socket and sends a POST header promising 5235 bytes, then sleeps without sending that body. Existing DDoS detection retained.
executable_review.cleanup: Method 163 at 0x2c3c removes installed-file/Run-value/startup-link artifacts and writes a delayed batch deleting Application.ExecutablePath and itself, configures hidden execution, then exits. Existing CIL self-image deletion-construction detection retained. Removal of a Run value does not establish a surviving persistence-installation path.
executable_review.plugins: Plugin, savePlugin and cached-plugin loading paths survive; injection/UAC/recovery names describe external plugin dispatch. Their implementations are absent, so no invented injection, escalation or credential-theft capability is added.
executable_review.overlay: A separate native Adobe Reader and Acrobat Manager 1.824.35.0289 executable begins at 0x27530. Its declared image and certificate occupy 1240656 bytes, followed by 400 bytes of repacker text. Existing overlay-decoy finding retained; all 342 findings on the embedded updater remain unchanged at 0 hostile/0 suspicious. A vendor component does not legitimize the damaged RAT containing it.
executable_review.judgment: Arbitrary shell and payload tasking, screen capture replies and threaded denial-of-service behavior tip the balance to malicious. Broken startup/configuration prevents claiming runtime operability, not identifying attack code. No authorization, invocation or original package provenance is supplied.

script_review.behavior: Both scripts read comma-separated ACCOUNTS/CANDIDATES and CLIENT_ID from environment. Outer loop chooses a candidate; inner loop submits it for every account to Microsoft organizations OAuth v2 token endpoint, password grant and Graph .default scope. JS awaits fetch and response.text; Python requests.post closes the response. Both discard tokens/results and have no exception handling.
script_review.judgment: The defining purpose is live password guessing across independent accounts. Likely malicious on a machine on balance, while an authorized audit remains possible; authorization, target ownership and invocation context are missing. Public registry origin and scanner scores do not decide this.
script_review.coverage_goal_exception: Only one distinct hostile behavior exists: OAuth password spraying. Existing bound-loop and Microsoft OAuth composite cover it. Source, facts and decoded-string review checked token theft/export, external exfiltration, staged execution, persistence, cleanup and evasion: none is implemented. Three to five hostile traits would duplicate the same attack or falsely promote neutral HTTP/form/environment operations. No rule addition is justified for either script.
script_review.verification: Python offline mock submits all four combinations for two accounts and two guesses, in candidate-major order, even though the replacement response has no token. JS control and data flow traced directly. No obfuscation or archive member exists.

rule_review.preservation: No rule removal, narrowing or severity reduction. Every original finding and embedded-member finding remains. Screenshot fallback preserves its original CopyFromScreen branch and adds a bounded SRCCOPY instruction path; stream and response locals remain bound.
rule_review.generalization: No hash, filename, exact specimen size, metadata-token number or configured endpoint is required. Shell task name is not pinned: renamed ExecTask still matches. New code sequences also match the separate v71 client; neutral module activation matches v3 and v71.
rule_review.consumers: Audited exact screenshot helper consumers and all ancestor directory selectors. New neutral deploy rule has no ancestor selector consumer. Broad collection/C2 consumers require independent webhook/OOB or CrystalX-specific context and did not gain findings on the originals.
tests: 16 CIL mutation/outside-batch controls passed, including wrong local, invalid heap reference, changed callee, absent receive/load/invoke, wrong SRCCOPY operation, different stream/response array, renamed file/task and benign managed controls. Existing v71 JPEG/Base64 and v3 JPEG/string detections retained.

The older mixed RAT/CI check passes its CIL cases but cannot complete its stale unrelated CI assertion: it references a missing hostile/github-actions-curl-token-exfil.yml; the present benign/ copy correctly lacks its expected hostile finding. No CI rule is changed.
rule_review.fixture: testdata/hostile/xworm-damaged-task-client.exe is the original first 0xfa00 bytes (64000): mapped damaged CLR image retained, appended vendor data omitted. It is explicitly a trimmed fixture, not the original executable.

remaining_disagreements: Both scripts retain hostile password-spray rules while calibrated atomscan labels remain benign: JS p=0.9890117, L=-1; Python p=0.9941581, L5000. PE remains hostile (p=0.99), level 85->25, confidence 86->92. Atomscan warns its v18 feature specification is older than v21. Source scans report flow-field-unavailable/flow-query-incomplete for some queries; direct source and bound AST spray detections establish these short programs. No remaining unsupported findings identified and no material detection loss.
